summary: xs-rs now negotiates PF_XATTRS with PF_XATTR_STREAM, carries extended attributes in DIR entries and DATA records in the C++ field order, applies them on both sides, and validates XATTR_START/CHUNK/END before any destination work. It interoperates with the parent C++ xs in both directions, including -X filtering and -XX internal names.
diagnosis: Most of the work was pinning the exact C++ ordering and rejection paths: xattrs follow filter-source in DIR entries, follow hard-link fields in DATA attributes, and precede DIR_CHILDREN in directory bodies. The parent's tests/xattrs_wire_test.py now passes 10/10 against the Rust binary, including oversized headers, duplicate references, unknown/out-of-order streams, incomplete attributes and corruption codes 11/12. No throughput benchmark was run; this step is protocol and metadata correctness.
change: Added rs/xs-rs/src/xattr.rs for Linux namespace rules, l*xattr access, XattrSet encoding/decoding and stream state. Extended Attrs/Options, protocol read_checked header bounds, DIR and DATA serialization, scan-time source reads, receiver validation/application/finalization, CLI -X/--xattrs/--no-xattrs, feature negotiation and XATTR_CONFIG. Added xattr rules to the filter list and integration tests in rs/xs-rs/tests/xattrs.rs.
expected_effect: A C++ client can push to or pull from xs-rs with -aX/-aXX and get identical user attributes, empty values, binary values, directory and file attributes, stale-attribute removal, and internal rsync names only at -XX. Attribute-only changes update metadata without resending file data and itemize with x; a second run is a no-op.
risks: Per-directory merge files that contain xattr rules are parsed but source xattr reads currently use the global filter context, so ': .rules' xattr exclusions are not applied per directory. Received stream values are held in memory (Linux values are at most 64 KiB); allocation is bounded and failure maps to the parent's file-I/O code. Interrupt/checkpoint behavior is unchanged.

commit_body: Add PF_XATTRS and PF_XATTR_STREAM, XATTR_CONFIG, and the streamed value frames to xs-rs. Encode and decode attributes in the C++ order for DIR entries and DATA records, apply them with Linux namespace and filter rules, and refuse malformed, unnegotiated, unreferenced, corrupted and incomplete streams before touching the destination. Cover C++ and Rust as client and server in interop tests, plus the parent's hostile wire suite.
